casa.source: lineage per the maintainer, confirmed while staging the E6000 for roc-ops/Portrayal#46 - Casa's cable assets (C100G, C40G, BDM2-M, SMM 300G-M) are Vistance property and the documentation now serves from vistancenetworks.com. The metal still says Casa Systems, which is why the directory does.

celestica.source: the name on the ES1010 and on its PSU FRU label

dell.source: the name on the metal. THE BRANDING MOVED TWICE AND THE HARDWARE DID NOT: PowerEdge shipped as Dell, then as Dell EMC after the 2016 EMC merger - the 14G bezel this library draws carries a DELL EMC wordmark - and the company now presents as Dell Technologies. The directory is `dell` because that is the constant across all three, and the aliases are here so a search for the name printed on a given year's chassis still lands.

cisco.source: the name on the metal; IOS XR makes it a software vendor too

edgecore.source: the hardware says so itself. `arcos-openconfig-components.json` from as7726-32x reports manufacturer "Accton" and platform "x86_64-accton_as7726_32x-r0", while the faceplate and the datasheets say Edgecore - the ODM parent and the brand it sells under. A DriveNets slide labelling one of these boxes "Vendor: Accton" is the same fact from the other direction.

juniper.source: the name on the metal; Junos makes it a software vendor too

readylinks.source: the wordmark printed on the GL-8xEP faceplate, in the vendor's own CAD export and product render. The catalogue is served from the vendor's own API and the datasheets from its own manifest, so the name is first-party throughout; no corporate lineage is known or claimed.

smartoptics.source: the name on the metal and on the DCP manuals

ufispace.source: the name on the metal and on the S9510-28DC hardware guide

accton.source: see edgecore - the box reports Accton as its own manufacturer

vistance.source: per the maintainer - holds the former Casa cable assets, and is the parent under which the Aurora Networks CMTS brand sits after CommScope (Jan 2026).

commscope.source: per the maintainer and roc-ops/Portrayal#47 - ARRIS was acquired by CommScope in 2019, and the CMTS line moved on to Vistance/Aurora in Jan 2026.

arris.source: per the maintainer and roc-ops/Portrayal#47 - acquired by CommScope, 2019

aurora-networks.source: per the maintainer and roc-ops/Portrayal#47 - the CMTS brand under Vistance from Jan 2026

arrcus.source: the running device says so: `arcos-show-version.txt` from a lab AS7726-32X, reads "Software: Arrcus ArcOS" with "Firmware MU: EdgeCore MU 1.2.3" beneath it - one line naming both the software house and the hardware one.

namespaces.common: shapes that stand for a class of part rather than one product
namespaces.std: apertures and cages conforming to spec/schemas/standards.yaml
